metadata.summary: European Solheim Cup players Lottie Woad and Charley Hull are six shots off the pace at the LPGA Tour's FM Championship with US team rival Allisen Corpuz holding a share of the lead heading into the weekend.

The English duo are tied 27th on three-under-par after Woad slipped back from a promising first round through a one-over 73 and Hull posted a two-under 70. But Corpuz shot a 67 to take a share of the lead with Japan's in-form Miyu Yamashita, last week's winner on the LPGA Tour, and Korea's Hyo Joo Kim on nine under. messages.text: Greaves denied by Cross in last-leg thriller on European Tour debut

metadata.summary: Beau Greaves took Rob Cross to a last-leg decider before losing out 6-5 on her European Tour debut in the first round of the Hungarian Darts Trophy.
metadata.content: Hungarian Darts Trophy: Beau Greaves just loses out to Rob Cross in last-leg decider on European Tour debut | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content Hungarian Darts Trophy: Beau Greaves just loses out to Rob Cross in last-leg decider on European Tour debut Beau Greaves became the first woman to play in a PDC European Tour event after qualifying for the Budapest tournament last month; Greaves and Rob Cross both averaged over 100 in first-round match with Cross edging the deciding leg after errors from opponent when left with chance on 70 Saturday 29 August 2026 01:05, UK Image: Rob Cross and Beau Greaves delivered a stunning round-one contest in Hungary (Gabor Kiss/PDC Europe image) Beau Greaves took Rob Cross to a last-leg decider before losing out 6-5 on her European Tour debut in the first round of the Hungarian Darts Trophy. Rising star Greaves, 22, made history by becoming the first woman to compete in a PDC European Tour event after qualifying last month for both this weekend's tournament in Budapest and the Czech Darts Open in September. And she pushed the experienced Cross to a deciding 11th leg in a thrilling tie on Friday evening, averaging an impressive match-best of 104.88 and hitting five 180s. messages.text: 'Box-office' Archer spell stirs 'relentless' England bowling display

metadata.summary: Jofra Archer bowled the fastest opening spell of his Test career as England produced a relentless, high-quality bowling display on day two of the second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s.
metadata.content: Jofra Archer: England's 'box-office' fast bowler touches 94 mph in blistering spell against Pakistan at Lord's | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Jofra Archer: England's 'box-office' fast bowler touches 94 mph in blistering spell against Pakistan at Lord's Mark Wood hails "high quality" England bowling performance as they dismiss Pakistan for 110 on day two of second Test at Lord's; Jofra Archer averages 90.7 mph in fastest opening spell of his Test career; Ollie Robinson is taking wickets at 8.84 a piece this summer Friday 28 August 2026 20:11, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the second day of the second Test between England and Pakistan at Lord’s. Jofra Archer bowled the fastest opening spell of his Test career as England produced a relentless, high-quality bowling display on day two of the second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s. England skittled the visitors for 110 in their first innings , with Ollie Robinson taking 4-11, Archer 3-26 and Josh Tongue 2-27, with Archer having set the tone with a blistering five-over burst before lunch that brought the opening breakthrough. According to CricViz , Archer's opening spell averaged 90.7 mph, with the odd delivery touching 94 mph. He picked up the flat-footed Shan Masood caught behind as Pakistan limped to lunch at 16-2 after 14.1 overs of superb pace bowling.
